absent: Numeric values of helper path limit, vmcore note size, profiling mode codes, and signal count are not shown.
Ownership, permissions, and teardown of sysfs group and proc entry beyond creation are not shown.
Sampling or interrupt mechanism consuming the profiler buffer is not shown.
Effects of RCU expedited and normal flags on grace periods are not shown.
Stop, park, bind, and cgroup wakeup signalling internals are not shown.
Delayed worker queue handling and work queuing or flushing APIs are not shown.
Scheduler, freezer, housekeeping mask, and hotplug ordering guarantees are not shown.

findings.text: Predicate decides whether kernel symbol values may be disclosed to a caller with given credentials. Unrestricted mode allows disclosure for performance use, intermediate mode requires a system logging privilege checked without auditing, and any other mode denies.
Byte order label has two build alternatives denoting little endian and big endian. The sysfs presentation uses the selected alternative as a newline terminated string.

Attribute helpers declare a static kernel object attribute whose identifier derives from the supplied name, one read only and one read write. Callers obtain paired show and optional store handlers through that naming rule.
Read handler exposes the global uevent sequence counter as an unsigned decimal value. It observes the counter atomically and formats one line of output.
Read handler exposes the build time CPU byte order label as text. Output is a single line containing the configured label.
Read handler exposes address width derived from pointer size scaled to bits. Result reflects the native pointer width of the running build.
Helper path attribute shows the current helper string and accepts bounded writes. Oversize writes are rejected, accepted bytes are copied and terminated, and a trailing newline is stripped.

Profiling sysfs control is once only. Read reports the enable flag. Write serializes concurrent attempts, refuses when already enabled, otherwise parses options, initializes the profiler buffer, registers proc state, and on success consumes the write.
Profiling enable path serializes with a function local mutex so option parsing and buffer initialization cannot interleave. The guard covers the enabled check and the subsequent setup sequence.

Profile option parser recognizes scheduler and virtualization mode keywords with an optional shift suffix, or a bare numeric shift. Shift values are clamped to the word width and the corresponding profiling mode is recorded with an informational message.

Profiler initialization derives bucket count from kernel text extent shifted by the configured amount, rejects a zero length with invalid argument and clears enablement, then attempts progressively more general allocations until one succeeds or reports out of memory.
Proc registration for profiling is a no op when disabled. When enabled it creates a world readable owner writable entry whose size accounts for a header plus one counter per bucket.
Read handler exposes crash dump note location as a physical address and a fixed note size. Address comes from the platform note accessor at read time.
Read handler exposes whether file capabilities are enabled as a decimal integer on one line.
Expedited RCU control is an integer sysfs value. Reads use a one time load, writes parse with base detection and reject unparsable input while accepting the byte count on success.
Normal RCU control mirrors the expedited control contract: single integer value, atomic read for display, strict numeric parse on store with invalid argument on failure.
Notes size denotes the extent between the linker provided notes section boundaries. Initialization uses it to decide whether a notes binary attribute exists and what size to advertise.
Global anchor holds the top level kernel kernel-object created during early sysfs initialization. Other kernel sysfs state hangs below this object.

Kernel attribute table always includes capability, sequence, byte order and address width entries, and conditionally includes helper, profiling, vmcore and RCU controls according to build options, terminated by null and wrapped in a single group.

Boot initializer creates the kernel object, attaches the attribute group, and when notes are present publishes them as a binary file backed by the notes start. Failures unwind in reverse order and log the error code.
Creation list spinlock protects the queue of pending kernel thread creation requests consumed by the daemon. Holders dequeue under lock and release it while spawning each thread.

Affinity mutex protects the global affinity list and preferred affinity installation. It serializes node default enrolment, preferred mask updates, and bulk housekeeping refreshes against concurrent topology changes.
Global holds the daemon task that serves all kernel thread creation. It is the parent context from which new kernel threads inherit initial state.

Creation request carries caller supplied identity and entry point plus placement hint, and a back channel for completion. Fields convey full name, function pointer, opaque argument, node, resulting task, completion object, and list linkage.

Per thread control block records flags, placement, lifecycle progress, entry point and argument, park and exit synchronization, optional block cgroup state, full name when truncated, owning task, affinity list linkage, and optional preferred mask.
Thread flag indices identify per CPU binding, pending stop request, and pending park request. Queries test these positions to report thread state.
Name accessor returns the stored full thread name when present, otherwise the task short name. Copies are bounded by caller supplied size with padding when using the full name.
Park queries report whether the park request flag is set, either for an explicit thread or for the caller. The explicit form is an internal helper and the caller form applies to current context.
Combined query reports whether current context has a stop or park request. Non thread callers observe false; thread callers observe the union of both request flags.
Freezable stop query enters the freezer when a freeze is pending, optionally reports whether freezing occurred, and then reports the stop request. Caller must allow sleeping.
Introspection helpers expose a thread entry point directly and its opaque argument through a fault tolerant copy. Non thread inputs yield null rather than failing.

Park handshake loops in a special parked state while the park request remains set, signalling arrival and sleeping without preemption, then returns to running once the request clears. Public entry applies the loop to current context.
Terminal helper optionally completes a caller supplied completion and then exits the calling thread with the supplied code, never returning.

Affinity resolution prefers an explicit mask when present, else node CPUs or housekeeping CPUs for unplaced threads, intersected with housekeeping and falling back to housekeeping when empty. Default enrolment registers the thread once and applies the computed mask unless bound or per CPU.
Per CPU query reports whether the flag marking CPU bound threads is set. Non thread inputs report false.

Thread trampoline adopts creation parameters, handles creator abandonment, resets scheduling to normal, publishes itself and sleeps until first wakeup, applies default affinity when eligible, honors early stop, synchronizes parking, runs the payload, and exits with its status.

Spawner records NUMA preference where supported and creates the thread sharing filesystem and file state with a child signal. On spawn failure it releases the name, and either frees the request when abandoned or reports the error through completion.
Mask binding applies a CPU mask while the target sleeps uninterruptibly and warns if the thread has already started. It is intended for use before first wakeup.

Creation daemon initializes its name, ignores signals, allows all memory nodes, opts out of freezing, initializes cgroup and affinity state, then sleeps while idle and drains the creation queue under lock, spawning each entry outside the lock.
Signal suppression marks every handler of a thread as ignored and then discards pending signals. It is used to give daemon and thread contexts a clean signal state.
Signal flush holds the signal handler lock with interrupts saved while clearing the pending flag and discarding both per thread and shared queues.

Preferred affinity installation requires the target to be inactive and unstarted and to have no prior preference. It allocates state, copies the mask, enrolls the thread once, recomputes effective affinity, and forces placement under the task lock.

Bulk affinity refresh skips work when no threads are enrolled, rejects bound or per CPU members, and otherwise refreshes masks. Forced refresh updates all members while unforced refresh limits work to threads with explicit preference or node placement.
Topology hooks route housekeeping changes to a forced refresh and CPU online events to an unforced refresh. Early init registers the online hook with the CPU hotplug facility.
Worker initializer clears the worker, initializes its raw spinlock with a caller supplied class and name, and sets up empty pending and delayed work lists.
Worker dispatch uses a raw spinlock with interrupts disabled to dequeue one item and publish it as current, and to clear ownership on stop. Payload execution itself runs without that lock.

Worker main loop adopts current as owner, marks freezable when requested, exits cleanly on stop, otherwise dequeues one unit of work and executes it with tracing, or sleeps when idle outside freezing, then handles freezing and rescheduling before repeating.

Worker factories allocate and initialize a worker, spawn its thread on a chosen node with formatted naming, record flags and ownership, and release on failure. CPU variant additionally binds the new worker to the requested CPU.
Profiling enablement can fail after partial setup and repeated writes always fail once enabled. Buffer sizing depends on shift clamping; an excessive shift yields zero length and disables profiling.

Helper and RCU stores validate length and numeric syntax and reject invalid input. Affinity installers warn on misuse such as started threads, duplicate preferences, or unexpected list membership, and bulk refresh reports invalid members without aborting.

Parking uses a special state with serialization against concurrent wakeups to avoid state corruption and to keep inactivity waits reliable. Node mask reads during enrolment race with CPU hotplug and rely on later migration or refresh to converge.
